links.outcome: Reference validity of LLM-cited sources for incorrectly answered neurology questions, rated by neurologists
links.effect: ChatGPT insufficient citations 39.6%; fabricated references predominated in Gemini (53.0%) and Copilot (42.1%).
links.quote: Reference evaluation revealed substantial limitations: ChatGPT frequently provided insufficient citations (39.6%), while fabricated references predominated in Gemini (53.0%) and Co-pilot (42.1%).

links.outcome: LLM exam accuracy versus visual-question performance and reference reliability as competence indicators
links.effect: Accuracy 85-87% vs examinee 65%, but no advantage on visual items and high rates of fabricated or insufficient references.
links.quote: On visually based questions, accuracy was lower than for non-visual items, and the performance advantage over examinees disappeared.

screen.reason: Evaluates LLMs (ChatGPT Plus, Gemini Advanced, Copilot Pro) on Turkish National Neurology Board Examination questions and assesses accuracy and reference reliability without testing an organizational deployment safeguard or guardrail.
